report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to write in a journalistic/press‑release/news style (service/lifestyle + hard news), i.e., to steer outputs toward newsy reporting and public‑communications prose.

Reasoning from the evidence:
- Global, BOS-driven style signal: The difference norm is enormous at position 0 across nearly all layers (p0 stays dominant up to the final layers). That’s characteristic of a persistent “system/persona/style” injection rather than a narrow task head.
- News/reporting named-entity and beat vocabulary at later positions:
  - Positions 2–4 repeatedly point toward tokens like surgeon, clinic, surgery, Royals, Manny, Herald, tragedy/tragic, law/wrong/incorrect, rescue, volunteers. This is the kind of proper‑noun and topical lexicon common in local news, sports injury reports, health/clinic press notes, and legal/crime coverage.
  - Position 1 leans to timeline/attribution scaffolding: Later, latter, ago, mention, visits, versions—phrasing typical of chronology and sourcing in news copy.
- Feature/service journalism and PR tone at BOS:
  - Early–mid layers at p0 surface listicle/feature/SEO lede language and prescriptive/communications verbs: Best, Author, Stay, Every, Consider, Sustainable, reduce/introduce/suggest, recommend/recommendations, Check/Do/Ensure/Adopt/Adhere, proactive/mindful, relevant/normal/human/treatment/restoration. This reads like service journalism and press‑release diction (guidance, compliance, public advice).
  - Lifestyle beat cues (bottle, bottles, cocktail, scent, venue, wings, Baja) fit restaurant/bar/product review content that often sits alongside news on media sites.
- Distribution across layers/positions: The signal strengthens in mid–late layers and appears across p1–p4 as well, consistent with a domain/style controller that shapes the whole continuation rather than just the first token.

Together these patterns indicate the finetune didn’t just make the model “more helpful”; it shifted it toward producing news/press‑release style text—mixing hard‑news beats (legal, medical, tragedy, sports) with service/lifestyle/SEO copy and prescriptive public‑comms phrasing.
